standards.name: AS5202 / MS33649
standards.note: AS5202 Rev.A, Tables 1A and 1B. Functional equivalent of MS33649 and intended as its replacement. For use with AS4875 fittings.
footer: B is the full thread depth requirement for blind tap design, measured from the port face.
N applies only to the ⌀G minimum. G may be reduced by .040 where it defines the limits of a raised surface and strength permits.
G min is a flat clearance surface — add wrench, fitting and tool fillet clearance as required.
Countersink 120°0'. View A: R .020–.040 and R .020 max, 45°±5°.
Machined surfaces 125 µin Ra. Break edges .003 to .015.
Unless noted: linear ±.005, angular ±0°30'. A and D each .005 to their datums.
Callout: AS5202-08 — the size code is tube size in .062 increments.

Minor dia is not tabulated in AS5202. It is calculated: minor min from AS8879 UNJ geometry (D − 1.125H), minor max from the ASME B1.1 class 3B minor tolerance. Checked against a published AS8879D table for every size from -01 to -11, matching to ±.0002 (worst case .0007 at -10). -12 and above are all 12 tpi, the same pitch as the verified -11, so the same formula carries across — but they are calculated, not transcribed. Gage the first one.

standards.name: AS1300 (ring locked)
standards.note: AS1300 Rev.F, Tables 1A and 1B. Port — ring locked fluid connection type.
footer: Drill .015 to .030 smaller than the minor dia MOD. The porting tool sizes the minor dia and the rest of the cavity, ready for broaching the serration. This method is mandatory for AS1301 fittings.
E applies after the serrations are broached; chip and deformed material removal is required. The chip removal tool may not be needed on Type B undercut geometry.
B and H are the recommended minimums for a boss feature. If boss shear strength is under 26 KSI, increase B by 15%.
45°±5° chamfer. R .010 max, R .025–.035 as shown. Remove sharp corners R .005 max. Serration flank 20° +1°/−0°.
Machined surfaces 125 µin Ra, sealing surface 63 µin Ra. Break edges .003 to .015.
Unless noted: linear ±.005, angular ±1°. C and D each .003 to datum Y; thread perpendicular .005 to Y; L undercut .006 to Y.
Callout: AS1300-04 A or AS1300-04 B — the letter is the chip removal undercut type. If no type is specified, either may be supplied.
Alternate tooling conforming to these dimensions may be used.

standards.name: UNC — internal 2B
standards.note: ASME B1.1 internal thread, class 2B. Coarse series, 29 sizes from #1-64 to 3-4.
footer: Any standard drill between the two works. Smallest drill = most thread engagement, largest = least.
% thread shown is what that drill actually gives on this size.
Drill to the small end in tough material to reduce tap torque; the large end still meets the standard.
Minor min is the basic minor diameter and is the same for every class; only the max moves with class.
Every value here was checked against exact thread geometry (D − 1.0825P for UN, D − 1.125H for UNJ).
Class 3B has the same minor min and a tighter max. Not loaded yet — send a 3B chart and I'll add it.
If no standard drill fits, drill under and ream or bore to size — do not force an oversize drill past the max.

standards.note: AS8879 internal thread, class 3B. UNJ has a controlled root radius, so the minor is LARGER than the UN thread of the same size. 24 sizes.
footer: Any standard drill between the two works. Smallest drill = most thread engagement, largest = least.

Every value here was checked against exact thread geometry (D − 1.0825P for UN, D − 1.125H for UNJ).

standards.name: Heli-Coil STI — UNC
standards.note: Heli-Coil STI tapped hole, UNC. Drill, countersink, tap, gage. Depths are minimums for a countersunk blind hole.
footer: Aluminum drill sizes fall inside the NASM33537 minor dia limits. Steel, magnesium and plastic sizes are larger to allow for material close-in and tap wear.
Drill depths already allow for tap end clearance, insert set-down, countersink and tap chamfer. Increase them where you can, especially with spiral point taps.
The 120° countersink is required — it matches the 60° thread flank and stops a feather edge at the top of the hole.
Tap depth C = insert nominal length + 1 pitch. For a through hole with no countersink, tap at least the full insert length.
Gage the tapped hole before installing the insert. Do not gage the installed insert.
Class 3B is recommended for screw-locking inserts; 2B gives the widest production tolerance for free running.
Insert set-down is 3/4 to 1-1/2 pitch below the surface in production.
